So crimes: extortion (illegal seizure of property by threat), robbery? They used threat of violence, but they didn't take directly by force? They forced him in taxi, threatened, got him to sign IOU and gave necklace as collateral. This is extortion (敲诈勒索). Also possibly illegal seizure of property (抢夺? but they used threat). Also "非法拘禁"? However typical Chinese law: extortion (敲诈勒索罪) involves using threats to obtain property. They threatened to beat him, forced him to sign IOU and give necklace. So extortion.

Also "抢夺" is taking property by force or threat in a short time. But they used threat and intimidation, not direct taking. So extortion.

Also "聚众斗殴" they later were suspected of that but not part of this case.

That could be considered illegal detention (非法拘禁) because they restricted his freedom of movement. However Chinese law: illegal detention requires depriving personal freedom by force, threat, or other means. Here they used threat and physical restraint (拽住). So could be illegal detention.
